adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36, app/models/post.rb:130-133, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — `cook_method: raw_html` makes `Post#cook` return unsanitized `raw`, and RSS content (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, no HTML sanitization) is stored then rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`: full stored-XSS on the Discourse origin for any content the configured RSS feed carries. (confidence=95, severity=P0)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook method that bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). The RSS job builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, meaning the stored `raw` is treated as already-rendered HTML. Finally, the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and for raw_html posts `post.cooked == post.raw` (also asserted in the new spec). Therefore any HTML/JS present in the configured feed content will be stored and emitted unsanitized under the Discourse origin, which is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130-137 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` splits the "cooked == sanitized" invariant into two silently-diverging paths distinguished only by an untyped int column, with no type-level marker at call sites like `post.cooked`. (confidence=90, severity=P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `cook_method` int column and changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) where sanitization would typically occur. The new import path (`TopicEmbed.import` / `PollFeed`) explicitly sets `cook_method: :raw_html` and feeds in HTML from external sources (RSS `i.content` and `Readability::Document#content`) with no sanitization step shown in the diff. Call sites still treat `post.cooked` as HTML-safe (e.g., `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`), so this does create silently divergent behavior keyed only by an integer flag, and it can violate the common expectation that "cooked" content is safe/sanitized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:39-43 — an on-demand single-URL retrieval synchronously runs the entire scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` job inline, blocking-fetching and importing every item in the whole configured feed just to resolve one requested URL, duplicating the hourly job's responsibility with no timeout handling. adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (before attempting to fetch the single `@embed_url`). adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — routing through `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` drops category assignment and original `created_at` (imports now get "now"), and creates hidden coupling where an already-poller-imported URL gets revised with readability-scraped content instead of the Disqus importer's own "[Permalink]" stub body. adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import logic changed from `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[Permalink](...)" , created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` (and a `--category` option) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` ultimately calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post via `PostCreator` without passing `created_at` or any category, so imported posts will default to “now” and cannot be placed into a chosen category anymore. Also, `TopicEmbed.import` de-dupes by `embed_url` and, when an embed already exists, revises the existing post if the SHA1 differs; thus running the Disqus importer for a URL already imported by the feed/embed pipeline would overwrite/revise that existing post with readability-scraped content rather than keeping the Disqus importer’s previous stub body. These behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-29 — check-then-act race: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `create!` inside `Topic.transaction`, racing the DB unique index on `embed_url` with no `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`; concurrent imports of the same URL raise uncaught. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it first does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if `embed.blank?`, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. Because `embed_url` has a unique index (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), two concurrent imports of the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/`StatementInvalid` exception. There is no `rescue`/retry or atomic `find_or_create_by`-style handling, so the exception would be uncaught here.

Under concurrency (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` running while `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` imports the same URL, or two pollers overlapping), both can observe no row and then both attempt `create!`, causing `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Neither `TopicEmbed.import` nor `Jobs::PollFeed` rescues this, so the exception would abort the `rss.items.each` loop and fail the job; with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, it will not be retried, effectively skipping remaining feed items for that run.

In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, `open(url).read` is also unrescued and will similarly raise on network/HTTP failures, propagating to callers (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, Disqus import task). (confidence=70, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that executes `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On many Postgres versions prior to “instant DEFAULT” behavior (and similarly older MySQL/InnoDB), adding a NOT NULL column with a non-null DEFAULT is implemented by rewriting the whole table and can take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE / metadata lock for the duration. This is a real operational/availability risk introduced by the change, especially for a typically large, frequently-written `posts` table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-52 — `Readability::Document.new` allowlists attribute names (`href`,`src`) but not values/schemes; a crafted `javascript:` href could survive extraction and execute in the Discourse origin when clicked, layered on top of the raw_html sanitizer bypass. (confidence=55, severity=P2)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches arbitrary remote HTML (`open(url).read`) and runs it through `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: %w[href src])`, which only restricts attribute *names* (href/src), not attribute *values/schemes*. The extracted `doc.content` is then passed into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `:raw_html` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. As a result, something like `<a href="javascript:...">` from the remote content can survive and be rendered in Discourse; clicking it would execute in the Discourse origin. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites href/src starting with `/` and does not neutralize `javascript:` schemes, so it doesn’t mitigate this.
